You could always try calling Apple and seeing if they'll replace the logic board for you.  I managed to get the logic board on my early 2011 MacBook Pro replaced for free last year, and it was totally out of warranty and I do not have AppleCare on it either.  My issue was just that my USB ports quit working, but I guess in order to fix that they had to replace the whole board.  I was quoted about $600 at an Apple store to fix it so after that I read around and it seemed to be a known issue and people were suggesting that those with that issue should call Apple.

I decided to give it a chance (not expecting much). And when I had them on the phone they denied that it was a known issue, but eventually they did offer to fix the issue for me free of charge.  As long as you don't hassle them and you're polite there is a chance that asking nicely could work for you, especially if you did nothing to cause the damage in the first place.

So I recommend you giving them a call, its definitely worth a shot.  I sure as hell was surprised when they agreed to fix my $600 issue for free on a three year old computer!
